title: Unit and quotient cocycle for the specified compact-support reduction maps
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, and fix one compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale site of each $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n B_{T,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $q_{m,n}:B_{T,m}\to B_{T,n}$ for quotient maps and $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ for their exact scalar restrictions [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Work in the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For arbitrary $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat R_X))$, put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}B_{X,n}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Define $\rho_{m,n}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ by the maps $P\otimes B_{X,m}\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(P\otimes B_{X,n})$, $x\otimes u\mapsto x\otimes q_{m,n}(u)$, on a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ of $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Use the scalar-unit-normalized derived tensor/restriction adjunction and write its unit as $\eta$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction].

These maps are independent of $P$. Their adjoints are the canonical isomorphisms $\beta_{m,n}:K_m\otimes^L_{B_{X,m}}B_{X,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$, represented by $(x\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto x\otimes q_{m,n}(u)v$, and $\rho_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\beta_{m,n})\eta_{K_m}$. They satisfy $\rho_{n,n}=1$ and $\rho_{r,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(\rho_{m,n})\rho_{r,m}$ for $r\geq m\geq n$.

Set $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and let $\sigma_{m,n}:F_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_n$ be the canonical proper/open scalar-restriction comparison [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. For $M_n=F_nK_n$ and $\tau_{m,n}=\sigma_{m,n,K_n}F_m(\rho_{m,n})$, one has $\tau_{n,n}=1$ and $\tau_{r,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(\tau_{m,n})\tau_{r,m}$ under the canonical restriction-composition identifications. No constructibility or Tor bound on $K$ is required.

proof.text: The coordinate module proves the identity and composition of the actual quotient ring maps and retains the canonical restriction identity/composition isomorphisms and the ordinary cochain computations unchanged; its module-specification body factors the same equations through reducible section-formula abbreviations.

For every flat-term K-flat P, the universal scalarReductionDerivedExistence witness says each homotopy counit is invertible. The cochain computation map is its composite with images of localization isomorphisms, hence is invertible. Construct the ordinary chain maps using their section formulas, then apply the separate universal-comparison theorem to these given maps. Combine these two facts with computation-map invertibility to prove compactSupportQuotient_representatives.

Apply the proved abstract adjunction calculation to the integral-to-m, integral-to-n and quotient adjunctions, with compactSupportRestrictionComp. It identifies the quotient adjunct with the canonical left-adjoint composition isomorphism, proving IsIso. The Hom equivalence apply_symm_apply identity gives the displayed rho = eta;Res(beta) equation. No representative or additional hypothesis is used.

The input identity and quotient composition laws hold for the prescribed rho maps in the canonical constant-coefficient presentation. The presentation-conversion lemma restates them with the original scalar-reduction functors, restriction functors and identification isomorphisms of the public statement; the canonical wrappers have exactly these values.

Apply the output identity conversion to the input identity: compact support with the normalized identity coefficient square transports the input identity, written with the original intrinsic compact-support functor, comparison and identity identification.

Apply the output composition conversion to the input laws: the transported cocycle of the native presentation, obtained from the published coefficient composition square with the quotient composite cast, naturality and functoriality, is restated with the original intrinsic compact-support expressions. Pair all clauses.
